analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: a date bump, a CI runner-routing wording change (Blacksmith to "macOS CI runners" with a link to build.md#ci-runner-routing), and a revised description of CI runner-routing checks (per-shard lanes, release workflows pinned to literal Blacksmith runners). The supplied units (head lines 457-1386) are unchanged test documentation around the changed hunks; the changed lines (1243-1244, 1808-1811) fall outside the supplied excerpt, but the patch excerpt is complete and shows they are prose only. I found no code, crypto, authorization, attestation, cache-storage or key-handling behavior change. The reviewed text does not relax any control in the threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012; T-041 prefix-cache sharing; T-053 authorization). It reiterates existing guidance: use isolated key namespaces, never use production cache roots or keys, and do not stop an operator process. One residual question for integration: the doc says release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners while the ci.yml macOS jobs now route through a separate CI plane. The actual routing implementation (workflow files, the routing script and its trust of the plane) is not in this batch. Any supply-chain or secret-exposure implications of routing CI jobs through that plane would need review in the workflow files themselves. The doc keeps release/signing jobs on literal runners, which is consistent with preserving the signing boundary, but that is unverified here. No finding is warranted on documentation alone.
